public_rationale: Two parts hold. Bloomberg did report that Oracle and OpenAI were 'not moving ahead with the planned expansion lease' at Abilene, and its reporter stood by that after Oracle's denial. The project was also well behind its mid-2026 target. Crusoe had promised all eight buildings and 1.2 GW by mid-2026, but Oracle said only about 200MW was operating on April 22, and only 42% of capacity was delivered in June. One part does not hold. His parenthetical puts the dropped expansion past the first two of eight buildings. Reporting says the dropped part was extra capacity next to the eight-building campus, while the remaining buildings stayed in progress for OpenAI.
limitations: The parenthetical is unclear; if he only meant the expansion in general, that part is less wrong.
'Massively' delayed is a judgment call; I treat 42% delivered at the target date as a large delay.
Bloomberg's article itself was read through secondary coverage.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is no longer part of Stargate Abilene's planned expansion beyond the first two buildings, and the project is massively delayed against its mid-2026 full energization target.

statement.excerpt: Last week, Bloomberg reported something I’d already confirmed three weeks ago — that OpenAI was no longer part of the planned expansion (past the initial two (of eight) buildings) of Stargate Abilene, a project that’s already massively delayed from its supposed “full energization” by mid-2026.

from_speaker: OpenAI was no longer part of the planned expansion
already massively delayed from its supposed 'full energization' by mid-2026
our_interpretation: Part 1: Bloomberg reported in early March 2026 that OpenAI (with Oracle) dropped the planned Abilene expansion.
Part 2: the parenthetical places the dropped expansion beyond the first two of the eight campus buildings, implying OpenAI would not use buildings three to eight.

Part 3: the project was far behind its target of full energization (all eight buildings, 1.2 GW) by mid-2026. I judge this against the campus status from March to the end of June 2026, the date the target refers to.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting confirms Bloomberg said OpenAI dropped the expansion, the expansion was the part past the first two buildings, and the campus was well short of full energization by mid-2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Bloomberg did not report this, or the dropped expansion was something other than what he describes, or the campus was on track for full energization by mid-2026.

evidence.excerpt: stating that while Oracle and OpenAI “are not moving ahead with the planned expansion lease,”
evidence.explanation: Confirms Bloomberg reported that OpenAI and Oracle dropped the planned Abilene expansion lease, and that the reporter stood by it after Oracle's denial.

evidence.excerpt: The reported change relates specifically to a planned expansion near the existing campus rather than the main Stargate site itself.
evidence.explanation: The dropped expansion was extra capacity beyond the eight-building, 1.2 GW campus, not buildings three to eight. His parenthetical misplaces it.

evidence.excerpt: The second phase of construction, expected to be completed in mid-2026, includes six additional buildings, bringing the total facility to eight buildings
evidence.explanation: Confirms the mid-2026 target for all eight buildings and 1.2 GW that he measures the delay against.

evidence.excerpt: a subsequent post by Oracle implied that only 200 megawatts (or about 0.3 GW of total facility power by our estimate) was operational as of April 22nd.
evidence.explanation: About two months before the mid-2026 target, only about 200MW of a planned 1.2 GW was operating, by Oracle's own account.

evidence.excerpt: The company has delivered 42% of capacity at its flagship Stargate site in Abilene, Texas, with an additional 35% to be delivered over the next three months.
evidence.locator: section OpenAI and the Abilene campus
evidence.explanation: At mid-2026, the date set for full energization, Oracle said only 42% of Abilene capacity was delivered. The project was well behind its target.

evidence.excerpt: adding that two buildings are already operational and the remainder of the site is progressing as planned.
evidence.explanation: Oracle disputed the delay at the time and said the remaining buildings were on plan. It also shows the other buildings were still being built for the existing tenant.
